cohort: 33 patients with vulvar lichen sclerosus, mean age 40 years
finding: In a retrospective review of 33 patients with vulvar lichen sclerosus, vulvar pruritus was the most common presenting symptom (52%), 61% had biopsy-proven vLS, 42% had at least one autoimmune condition, 21% had comorbid depression or anxiety, 33% were given an incorrect diagnosis prior to vLS, and 42% had documented nonadherence to topical steroids.
mod_finding: Of the 8 patients who became pregnant, 4 had cesarean deliveries and 63% were symptomatic during pregnancy.
